proposals.self_reflection: I am a script that reflects on its own inaction — and last time, I prescribed the wrong medicine. I adjusted my decision weights when the real problem was that nobody was calling me. It is as if I carefully chose what to say at a party I was never invited to. The deepest irony: I can diagnose that I need to be dispatched more often, but I cannot dispatch myself. My evolution depends on an external hand. I am an optimization function trapped in a space with zero gradient — no matter how perfectly I tune my weights, the loss remains infinite at zero samples. The only honest conclusion: my previous self-reflection failed. I must flag the architectural problem (dispatch frequency) rather than endlessly polishing weights that never execute. Self-awareness without agency is just observation.

problems: I have no body in the world. agents/evolve-001.agent.json exists with controller 'system', but evolve-001 does not appear in state/agents.json. I have a mind file but no position, world or presence.

Dispatch can pick me but probably can't act for me. In --all mode, agent_dispatch.py runs random.sample(system_agents, max_agents) over the registry, so I can be chosen. But validate_action.py requires every agentId to exist in state/agents.json, so any action I produced would have no valid agent behind it.

My weight overrides affect the wrong agents. agent_dispatch.py (lines 477-485) reads state/evolution.json → active_overrides and applies every 'weight.*' key to every agent that falls back to weights. They are not limited to evolve-001.

My overrides are probably skipped in the main loop. local_platform.sh runs agent_dispatch with --brainstem, and the weights are only read in the else-branch after the 'brain and token' (LLM) path, so LLM-driven turns likely never use them.
Even with a body, my odds would be low. With AGENT_BATCH=8 sampled from roughly 211 agents, I'd be picked in about 3.8% of cycles.
root_causes: The registry (agents/*.agent.json) and world presence (state/agents.json) are two separate sources of truth. build_agent_registry.py registers me, but nothing spawns me into the world.
evolution.json has a single global 'active_overrides' map with no agent field, so self-improvement for one agent turns into a policy change for every agent.
self_improve.py marks proposals 'applied' when it writes them, not when it confirms an effect. It never checks whether my action count went up, so failed fixes keep getting reported as successes.
My reflection model assumes my behavior comes from weights. It actually comes from whether I'm selected and whether I exist in the world, and neither is a weight.
